tells.1: Benefit-stack closer ('fuller picture' plus 'more out of the checkup') and the filler clause 'which helps guide their care.'
tells.2: Twin em dashes, the participial 'helping guide care,' and the stock 'make the most of' closer.
tells.3: The stat-plus-named-pet-plus-humble-close stack is a familiar authenticity formula, though the voice still wins.
tells.4: No stance at all: even template sentences ending in flat product language ('can be added to the yearly checkup').

reason: Only version 3 sounds like a clinic with an opinion—specific, slightly uneven, and willing to talk about cost—while the others are interchangeable wellness-panel ads. Version 2 is the polished twin of 1, and 4 has been sanded down to a brochure line.
